SMTO-MON-0005 — This monitor has used up its model checks

GUID: 4fa24df4-254a-4abb-bc1f-ed2c31459497
Slug: monitor-inference-budget-exhausted
Domain: MON · Subsystem: mon

What happened

  • This monitor has used all the model judgments it's allowed, so it can't ask the model to judge new readings. It keeps collecting readings, and earlier results are kept.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask the agent to show this monitor's status and readings. The readings collected so far are still saved and may already answer your question.
  2. If you still need the model to judge new readings, ask the agent to start a new monitor for the same check. The allowance belongs to each monitor, so a new monitor starts with a fresh one.
  3. Where you can, use a plain condition, such as disk use above 90%, instead of a judgment described in words. Plain conditions are checked without the model, so they don't use up this allowance.

What success looks like

  • The monitor's readings are visible, and any new monitor reports judged results.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't change unrelated time limits or budget settings to fix this; they don't change this monitor's allowance.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • reserve_native_judgement declined a semantic judgment because the monitor's native_inference_calls reached native_monitor_max_model_calls (default 32); observation collection continues.

What this means

  • Atomic judgment reservation compares the lifetime count with its configured inference limit and declines another reservation at the limit. Monitor validation does not execute the observation command. Existing monitor state and stored observations remain authoritative; missing planning support or exhausted judgment budget does not prove observation collection failed.

Why this can happen

  • Atomic judgment reservation compares the lifetime count with its configured inference limit and declines another reservation at the limit.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the lifetime judgment count and allowance separately from observation collection state.

How to fix it

  • Review existing observations (monitor.inspect with operation=observations). If more semantic evaluation is intended, create a new monitor (the counter is per monitor, stored in its context) or use a deterministic condition; the cap is native_monitor_max_model_calls in the monitor context. See reserve_native_judgement in src/agent_runtime/monitors/store.py.
  • Inspect existing observations and monitor budget. Create or adjust a monitor only when additional semantic evaluation is intended.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Observations remain available and further judgments occur only under an intentionally supported budget decision.

What not to do

  • Do not change an unrelated timeout, budget or policy. Check whether the named setting applies only to a new task.

Technical notes

  • Monitor validation does not execute the observation command. Existing monitor state and stored observations remain authoritative; missing planning support or exhausted judgment budget does not prove observation collection failed.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
